issues.description: PR does three unrelated things; should be three patches
issues.detail: One patch claims to add POST tests, but also rewrites the README example with wholesale style/formatting churn (parenthesized imports, format() vs %, code_to_http_status, handle() signature change, bounded_stream swap), and adds an FAQ entry. THREE-PATCHES. The README signature change for StorageError.handle reorders (ex, req, resp, params) to (req, resp, ex, params) which is a semantic change buried in a 'test' PR. Refuse and split.

issues.description: stream.read() -> bounded_stream.read() is a behavior change disguised as a test fix
issues.detail: examples/things_advanced.py swaps req.stream.read() for req.bounded_stream.read(). The PR description even says the intended change was to add req.content_length to stream.read(), which is a different fix. Pick one. The commit message lies about what the diff does. BAD-TASTE. State the actual reason for the swap or revert it.

issues.description: FAQ example is buggy and won't behave as the test claims
issues.detail: PostTest.on_post does `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)` with Content-Length: 1 and empty body. read(1) on an empty bounded stream returns b'', so the test passes by accident, not by design. The example purports to demonstrate header override but actually demonstrates a read-past-EOF coincidence. Rewrite so the assertion follows from the logic, not from luck.

issues.description: Tests have no assertions on response body, only status codes
issues.detail: resp3 asserts 201 but doesn't verify Location header or that the thing was actually stored. resp4 asserts 400 but doesn't check which 400 fired (empty-body vs malformed-JSON vs missing-thing). A test that can't distinguish between three different failure modes isn't testing the example, it's testing that something went wrong. Add body/title assertions.

issues.description: FAQ code sample has style inconsistencies and a stray trailing comma
issues.detail: `headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),]` — gratuitous trailing comma in a one-element list reads as accidental. `assert(result.status == ...)` uses assert-as-function, which is a common Python footgun (assert is a statement; the parens make it a tuple in other contexts). Match the rest of the docs' style.

issues.description: FAQ example class missing falcon route handler conventions and docstring
issues.detail: PostTest is presented as a pedagogical example but has no docstring explaining what it demonstrates, and the control flow (nested if/else returning three different statuses) is harder to read than it needs to be. For an FAQ entry teaching header simulation, the example resource should be the smallest thing that demonstrates the point.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK bordering on REFUSE. The PR title says "add POST tests" but the diff bundles three unrelated changes: a test addition, a behavior change to the example (stream -> bounded_stream), and a sweeping README restyle including a method-signature reorder for StorageError.handle. That's THREE-PATCHES at minimum. The tests themselves are weak — status-code-only, no body or header assertions, can't distinguish failure modes. The FAQ example passes by accident (read-past-EOF returns b''), not by the logic it claims to demonstrate. Split the patches, tighten the assertions, and fix the FAQ sample so the test result follows from the code.
